question: The region of the Earth's atmosphere where weather events occur is known as the:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Troposphere**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **troposphere** is the lowest layer of the Earth's atmosphere and extends from the Earth's surface up to an average height of about **8–15 km**, depending on the latitude and season.
 
• This layer contains approximately **75% of the atmosphere's mass** and nearly all of its **water vapor**, making it crucial for weather phenomena.
 
• Weather events such as **rain, snow, storms, and winds** occur in the troposphere due to the presence of water vapor and temperature variations.
 
• The temperature in the troposphere generally decreases with altitude, at an average rate of **6.5°C per kilometer** (known as the lapse rate).
 
• The boundary between the troposphere and the stratosphere is known as the **tropopause**, which acts as a barrier preventing the mixing of air between the two layers.
 
• This layer also plays an important role in the **Earth’s climate system**, as it contains the greenhouse gases that regulate surface temperatures.
 
• The troposphere is where human activities such as aviation and pollution primarily occur, influencing its composition and dynamics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mesosphere**__

 __
 
• The **mesosphere** is the third layer of the atmosphere, located above the stratosphere and below the thermosphere.
 
• It extends from about **50 to 85 km** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It is the coldest atmospheric layer, with temperatures dropping as low as **-90°C**.
 
• This layer is where **meteors burn up** upon entering the Earth's atmosphere, creating shooting stars.
 
 
 
• **Stratosphere**__
 __
 
• The **stratosphere** lies above the troposphere and extends from about **15 to 50 km** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It contains the **ozone layer**, which absorbs and scatters ultraviolet solar radiation, protecting life on Earth.
 
• In contrast to the troposphere, the temperature in the stratosphere **increases with altitude** due to the absorption of UV radiation by ozone.
 
• This layer is also relatively stable, making it suitable for **commercial aviation**.
 
 
 
• **Exosphere**__
 
 
• The **exosphere** is the outermost layer of the atmosphere, extending from about **500 km** above the Earth's surface to the edge of space.
 
• This layer contains very few air molecules and is where **satellites orbit**.
 
• The particles in the exosphere can escape into space due to the **low gravity pull** at these altitudes.
